# A `from_credit:` payment block carrying a `Transaction` / `PaymentSplit`
# directive.
#
# There is no grouped spelling of a credit block. `Transaction` /
# `PaymentSplit` is read by the branch that links a bank transaction, and a
# block saying `from_credit:` goes to the one that spends an owner's credit,
# which knows only `txn_guid:` and `txn_split_guid:` — one split each. So the
# directive is read by nobody.
#
# It is not simply ignored, either, which is what makes it worth refusing:
# `payment_slots` counts a settlement per `PaymentSplit` whatever kind of block
# it sits in, so the two halves of the run disagree about how many settlements
# this file accounts for while the money path reads none of them.
#
# A line the file states and the run ignores is what every other unread line in
# this format is refused for.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming `from_credit:`, and a book the
# run has not touched.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    amount: 100
    from_credit: #True
    credit_dated: 2026-02-27
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
